description: Ford's massive pushrod V8 designed for heavy-duty truck applications. At 7.3 liters (445 cubic inches), it's the largest displacement gasoline engine Ford currently produces. Despite its truck origins, the Godzilla has become incredibly popular in the performance community for its massive displacement and modification potential.

heritage.significance: First new pushrod Ford V8 design since the 385 series, designed for ultimate durability
innovations: Cam-in-block OHV design for maximum torque
heritage.design_philosophy: Built for work truck durability with 250,000+ mile service life in mind

variants.notes: Ford Performance 'Megazilla' crate engine with ported heads and aggressive cam

common_issues.description: Engine is relatively new with no widespread issues reported

strengths: Simple pushrod design - easy to work on

naturally_aspirated.bolt_ons: Intake, headers, cam swap can yield 500+ HP
naturally_aspirated.ported_heads: With ported heads and cam (Megazilla-style), 600+ HP possible
naturally_aspirated.notes: Very responsive to traditional V8 modifications

forced_induction.supercharger: Whipple and other manufacturers offer kits for 700-1000+ HP
forced_induction.turbo: Twin turbo kits available, 800-1200+ HP possible
forced_induction.notes: Factory internals handle moderate boost well

notes.swap_popularity: The Godzilla has become extremely popular for engine swaps into classic trucks, hot rods, and even Broncos. Ford Performance offers a crate engine and control pack.
notes.traditional_v8_feel: Despite being modern, the pushrod design gives the Godzilla traditional American V8 character that many enthusiasts appreciate.
notes.megazilla: Ford Performance's Megazilla crate engine comes ready to make 615 HP with no forced induction - impressive for a naturally aspirated pushrod engine.
